newsitem.title: INDIA: India rulers, Congress resume talks on eve of vote.
newsitem.headline: India rulers, Congress resume talks on eve of vote.

text.p: India's governing coalition and the Congress party on Thursday began a second round of crucial talks on the eve of a vote of confidence, after a split on who should lead the nation.

The first round of talks on Wednesday failed to make headway after Congress, which has threatened to help topple Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda in Friday's vote, insisted its leader, Sitaram Kesri, be named prime minister.
Kesri, citing a drifting economy and rising communal tensions, withdrew his party's support for Deve Gowda on March 30, triggering the political crisis and raising the prospect of mid-term elections.
Deve Gowda proposed the confidence vote after President Shankar Dayal Sharma asked him to prove his majority in parliament.

The centre-left coalition has insisted that Deve Gowda remain Prime Minister. "The United Front delegates summarily rejected the (Congress) suggestion," a senior United Front official said on Wednesday.
Each side was represented by five members at the first round of talks at the New Delhi residence of Jammu and Kashmir state chief Farooq Abdullah.

"Let us see how the discussion goes on," senior Congress leader Ved Prakash told Reuters on Thursday when asked whether Congress would continue to insist on Kesri's elevation to the prime ministership.
Kesri hosted a dinner on Wednesday for Congress deputies in parliament in a bid to display party unity.
"There will be a revolt in Congress if the negotiations fail," the United Front official said.

Both United Front and Congress leaders said they were hopeful a solution would be found to avert snap polls which opinion surveys show would likely strengthen the rightwing opposition Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
"Both sides are keen that a solution should evolve," said Prakash. "Nobody wants elections. They feel that secular forces should come together otherwise the advantage would go to the BJP."
The Hindu nationalist BJP emerged as the largest single party in parliament in inconclusive elections last year. With its allies, it controls 193 seats.
The 15-member United Front has 180 deputies in the 542-member lower house of parliament, the Lok Sabha, while the Congress has 140 legislators.

The Lok Sabha was set to convene on Friday at 11 a.m. (0530 GMT) and was expected to debate the confidence motion before taking a vote. The prime minister would need a simple majority of those present and voting to win.
Many politicians feel President Sharma would invite the BJP to form a government if Deve Gowda lost the vote.
The BJP ruled for 12 days last May, then quit after it failed to muster a majority, paving the way for Deve Gowda to assume power.
